ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \triangle ABC\cong \triangle AED$, with point E on line segment BC, and $ \angle 1=56^\circ$, what is the measure of $ \angle AED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle AED$,\\
then $\angle BAC=\angle EAD$, and $AB=AE$,\\
thus $\angle BAE=\angle 1=56^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle B=\angle AEB=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-56^\circ)=62^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle AED=\angle B=\boxed{62^\circ}$.

According to the corresponding order, it can be known that A corresponds to A, B corresponds to E, and C corresponds to D. Therefore ∠BAC = ∠EAD, and AB = AE; the required ∠AED corresponds to ∠ABC. Also because ∠BAC = ∠BAE + ∠EAC, ∠EAD = ∠EAC + ∠CAD, the two are equal, subtracting the common angle ∠EAC gives ∠BAE = ∠CAD = 56°. In triangle ABE, AB = AE, so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal: ∠ABE = ∠BEA = (180° − 56°) / 2 = 62°. Since B, E, C are collinear, ∠ABE and ∠ABC are the same, so ∠ABC = 62°. method.method_draft: First read the diagram: B, E, C lie on one straight horizontal segment with E between B and C; from A there are rays to B, E, C, and D; the marked angle 1 is the angle between AC and AD, so ∠CAD = 56°. From the text, use the congruence order ΔABC ≅ ΔAED, so A corresponds to A, B to E, and C to D. Therefore ∠BAC = ∠EAD and AB = AE, and also the desired ∠AED corresponds to ∠ABC. Since ∠BAC and ∠EAD both include the common angle ∠EAC on opposite decompositions, subtract ∠EAC from both: ∠BAE = ∠CAD = 56°. In triangle ABE, AB = AE, so it is isosceles and its base angles are equal: ∠ABE = ∠BEA = (180° − 56°)/2 = 62°. Because B, E, C are collinear, ∠ABE is the same as ∠ABC. Finally, by congruence, ∠AED = ∠ABC = 62°.
